```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

Rascher et al. (2025) re-estimated the adult empagliflozin population PK and
HbA1c exposure-response models (Baron 2016) on the paediatric DINAMO trial in
a Bayesian (NUTS) framework. The analysis was sequential: the popPK model was
fitted first, each patient's steady-state AUC was computed as daily dose /
individual CL/F, and that AUC then drove the HbA1c model. The package
therefore ships two models:

* `Rascher_2025_empagliflozin` -- two-compartment popPK with sequential
  zero-order / first-order absorption.
* `Rascher_2025_empagliflozin_hba1c` -- indirect-response HbA1c model driven
  by the `AUC_EMPA` covariate.

```{r load-models}
mod_pk <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rascher_2025_empagliflozin"))
mod_pd <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Rascher_2025_empagliflozin_hba1c"))
```

* Citation: `r mod_pk$reference`
* PK description: `r mod_pk$description`
* PD description: `r mod_pd$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/bcp.70096> (open access, PMC12304805)

# Population

DINAMO randomised young people aged 10-17 years with type 2 diabetes. The PK
analysis used 223 quantifiable concentrations from 74 patients on empagliflozin
10 mg (n = 46), 25 mg (n = 16) or 10 mg re-randomised to 25 mg (n = 12)
(Table 1). Table S2 gives a median weight of 90.0 kg (42.5-169), median age
14.5 years (10-17) and median eGFR of 125 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (89.7-241, Zappitelli
equation); Table S1 gives 62.2% female, 50.0% White, 32.4% Black and 5.4%
Asian. The HbA1c analysis used 394 observations from 103 patients: placebo
(n = 51), empagliflozin 10 mg (n = 39) and 10 mg then 25 mg from week 15
(n = 13). 49.4% had background insulin and 90.3% background metformin
(Results, Table 2).

```{r population}
str(mod_pk$population[c("n_subjects", "age_range", "weight_range", "sex_female_pct")])
str(mod_pd$population[c("n_subjects", "dose_range", "co_medication")])
```

# Pharmacokinetics

## Virtual cohort

200 virtual patients per dose (10 mg and 25 mg once daily), with weight,
eGFR, sex and race drawn to match Tables S1 and S2. Weight and eGFR are
log-normal around the DINAMO medians, truncated to the observed ranges.

```{r pk-cohort}
set.seed(2025)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2025)
n_arm <- 200
make_cov <- function(n, id0) {
  race <- sample(c("other", "black", "asian"), n, replace = TRUE, prob = c(0.622, 0.324, 0.054))
  data.frame(
    id = id0 + seq_len(n),
    WT = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(90), 0.27)), 42.5), 169),
    CRCL = pmin(pmax(exp(rnorm(n, log(125), 0.18)), 89.7), 241),
    SEXF = rbinom(n, 1, 0.622),
    RACE_BLACK = as.integer(race == "black"),
    RACE_ASIAN = as.integer(race == "asian")
  )
}
cohort <- rbind(
  cbind(make_cov(n_arm, 0), dose = 10),
  cbind(make_cov(n_arm, n_arm), dose = 25)
) |>
  mutate(treatment = paste(dose, "mg QD"))

tau <- 24
n_dose <- 10
t_last <- (n_dose - 1) * tau
obs_t <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), t_last + seq(0, 24, by = 0.25))))

# rate = -2 makes rxode2 infuse each dose into the depot over the modelled D1.
ev_pk <- bind_rows(
  cohort |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = (0:(n_dose - 1)) * tau) |>
    mutate(amt = dose, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", rate = -2),
  cohort |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_t) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", rate = 0)
) |>
  arrange(id, time, desc(evid))

sim_pk <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, events = ev_pk, returnType = "data.frame",
                          keep = "treatment")
sim_pk <- left_join(sim_pk, select(cohort, id, dose), by = "id")
```

## Concentration-time profiles at steady state

```{r pk-profile}
sim_pk |>
  filter(time >= t_last) |>
  group_by(treatment, tad = time - t_last) |>
  summarise(med = median(Cc), lo = quantile(Cc, 0.05), hi = quantile(Cc, 0.95), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, med, colour = treatment, fill = treatment)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Empagliflozin (nmol/L)",
       title = "Simulated steady-state profiles (median, 5th-95th percentiles)")
```

## Steady-state AUC: closed-form check and Figure 3

At steady state AUC over the dosing interval equals dose / CL/F exactly, which
is how the authors derived AUCss. The trapezoidal AUC of the simulated
profiles must reproduce it; both sides use the same subject parameters, so the
only difference is the 0.25-h trapezoid and integrator error.

```{r auc-closed-form}
mw <- 450.91
auc_ss <- sim_pk |>
  filter(time >= t_last) |>
  group_by(id, treatment, dose) |>
  summarise(
    auc_trap = sum(diff(time) * (head(Cc, -1) + tail(Cc, -1)) / 2),
    cl = cl[1],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(auc_cf = dose * 1e6 / mw / cl)
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_ss$auc_trap / auc_ss$auc_cf - 1) < 0.01))

auc_ss |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(median_AUCss = median(auc_cf), q25 = quantile(auc_cf, 0.25),
            q75 = quantile(auc_cf, 0.75), median_CL = median(cl), .groups = "drop") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 2))
```

Figure 3 of the paper shows simulated paediatric AUCss for 10 mg once daily
with a median of about 2300 nmol*h/L and an interquartile range of about
1800-2950 nmol*h/L (digitised by the maintainers).

```{r fig3}
ggplot(filter(auc_ss, dose == 10), aes(x = "Paediatric (10 mg)", y = auc_cf)) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "#5ec8cc") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 2300, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Empagliflozin AUCss (nmol*h/L)",
       title = "Replicates Figure 3 of Rascher 2025 (paediatric arm)",
       caption = "Dashed line: published median, digitised (about 2300 nmol*h/L).")

med_10 <- median(auc_ss$auc_cf[auc_ss$dose == 10])
stopifnot(abs(med_10 / 2300 - 1) < 0.15)
```

## NCA with PKNCA

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim_pk |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
dose_df <- ev_pk |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id,
                             concu = "nmol/L", timeu = "h")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id, doseu = "mg")
intervals <- data.frame(start = t_last, end = t_last + tau,
                        cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

reference <- data.frame(treatment = "10 mg QD", auclast = 2300)
nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  nca_res, reference, by = "treatment",
  params = c("cmax", "tmax", "cmin", "auclast"),
  units = c(cmax = "nmol/L", tmax = "h", cmin = "nmol/L", auclast = "nmol*h/L"),
  label_first_column = "NCA parameter"
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The paper reports no NCA table; the only published reference is the
digitised Figure 3 median AUCss at 10 mg (shown as AUC over the dosing
interval at steady state).

The full simulated steady-state NCA summary by dose:

```{r pknca-summary}
knitr::kable(summary(nca_res))
```

# HbA1c exposure-response

## Typical-value time course (Figure S3)

A typical paediatric patient with eGFR 125 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (truncated to 120
in the model), observed baseline HbA1c equal to the model baseline, and AUCss
2300 nmol*h/L (the Figure 3 median at 10 mg), simulated on placebo and on
empagliflozin with and without background insulin. Time 0 is the baseline
HbA1c observation.

```{r pd-typical}
mod_pd_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_pd)
wk <- c(0, 4, 12, 26)
typ <- tidyr::crossing(insulin = 0:1, auc = c(0, 2300)) |>
  mutate(id = row_number())
ev_typ <- typ |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = seq(0, 26 * 168, by = 24)) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, cmt = "Hba1c", CONMED_INSULIN = insulin, AUC_EMPA = auc,
         HBA1C = 7.35 * 1.15^insulin, CRCL = 125)
sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pd_typ, events = ev_typ, returnType = "data.frame",
                           keep = c("insulin", "auc"))
pbo_adj_typ <- sim_typ |>
  select(time, insulin, auc, Hba1c) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = auc, values_from = Hba1c, names_prefix = "auc_") |>
  mutate(pbo_adj = auc_2300 - auc_0, week = time / 168,
         group = ifelse(insulin == 1, "Baseline insulin", "No baseline insulin"))

ggplot(pbo_adj_typ, aes(week, pbo_adj)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~group) +
  labs(x = "Time (week)", y = "Placebo-adjusted HbA1c change (%)",
       title = "Typical paediatric patient, 10 mg (compare Figure S3, median line)")

wk26 <- filter(pbo_adj_typ, time == 26 * 168) |> select(group, pbo_adj)
knitr::kable(wk26, digits = 3)
```

Figure S3 / Figure 4 show paediatric median placebo-adjusted changes at week
26 of about -1.07% with baseline insulin and -0.70% without (digitised). The
typical patient reproduces both within 10%:

```{r pd-typical-check}
ref_fig4 <- c(`Baseline insulin` = -1.07, `No baseline insulin` = -0.70)
rel <- wk26$pbo_adj / ref_fig4[wk26$group] - 1
stopifnot(all(abs(rel) < 0.10))
```

The placebo course of the insulin group carries the disease progression: the
typical HbA1c rises by about 1.1 percentage points over 26 weeks, matching the
prediction-corrected placebo change from baseline of about +1% at 4400 h in
Figure 2B.

```{r pd-progression}
sim_typ |>
  filter(auc == 0, time %in% (wk * 168)) |>
  group_by(insulin) |>
  reframe(week = time / 168, cfb = Hba1c - Hba1c[1]) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = week, values_from = cfb, names_prefix = "week_") |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Placebo-adjusted change in a virtual cohort (Figure 4)

Figure 4 shows the distribution of each simulated patient's placebo-adjusted
change. Each virtual patient is solved twice -- on placebo and on 10 mg --
with the same random effects, by drawing the BASE / PROG etas outside rxode2
and passing them as parameters to the zero-random-effect model. Each patient's
AUCss is dose / CL/F from the 10-mg PK cohort above, and the observed baseline
HbA1c covariate is set to the patient's model baseline.

```{r pd-cohort}
om <- mod_pd$omega
set.seed(26)
pd_cohort <- auc_ss |>
  filter(dose == 10) |>
  select(id, auc = auc_cf) |>
  left_join(select(cohort, id, CRCL), by = "id") |>
  slice(rep(seq_len(n()), 2)) |>
  mutate(insulin = rep(0:1, each = n_arm), pid = row_number())
# Base-R draws (set.seed) keep the cohort identical across rxode2 builds.
etas <- matrix(rnorm(2 * nrow(pd_cohort)), ncol = 2) %*% chol(unclass(om)[1:2, 1:2])
pd_cohort$etalrbase <- etas[, 1]
pd_cohort$etadp_slope <- etas[, 2]
pd_cohort$HBA1C <- 7.35 * 1.15^pd_cohort$insulin * exp(pd_cohort$etalrbase)

paired <- bind_rows(
  mutate(pd_cohort, arm = "placebo", AUC_EMPA = 0),
  mutate(pd_cohort, arm = "empagliflozin", AUC_EMPA = auc)
) |>
  mutate(sid = row_number())
ev_pd <- paired |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = wk * 168) |>
  transmute(id = sid, time, evid = 0L, cmt = "Hba1c", CONMED_INSULIN = insulin,
            AUC_EMPA, HBA1C, CRCL) |>
  arrange(id, time)
# `params` rows are matched to subjects in order, so both frames are sorted by id.
prm <- transmute(paired, id = sid, etalrbase, etadp_slope) |>
  arrange(id)
sim_pd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pd_typ, events = ev_pd, params = prm,
                          returnType = "data.frame")
sim_pd$id <- as.integer(as.character(sim_pd$id))
sim_pd <- sim_pd |>
  left_join(select(paired, id = sid, pid, arm, insulin, HBA1C), by = "id")
# Each subject must carry its own eta: the solved baseline equals the
# baseline built from that subject's eta draw.
chk_base <- filter(sim_pd, time == 0)
stopifnot(max(abs(chk_base$rbase / chk_base$HBA1C - 1)) < 1e-8)

pbo_adj <- sim_pd |>
  select(pid, insulin, arm, time, Hba1c) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = arm, values_from = Hba1c) |>
  mutate(pbo_adj = empagliflozin - placebo,
         group = ifelse(insulin == 1, "Baseline insulin", "No baseline insulin"))

wk26_cohort <- pbo_adj |>
  filter(time == 26 * 168) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(median = median(pbo_adj), q25 = quantile(pbo_adj, 0.25),
            q75 = quantile(pbo_adj, 0.75), .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(wk26_cohort, digits = 3)

ggplot(filter(pbo_adj, time == 26 * 168), aes(group, pbo_adj, colour = group)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  geom_point(data = data.frame(group = names(ref_fig4), pbo_adj = ref_fig4),
             shape = 4, size = 4, colour = "black") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Placebo-adjusted HbA1c change from baseline (%)",
       title = "Replicates Figure 4 of Rascher 2025 (paediatric, 10 mg, week 26)",
       caption = "Crosses: published medians, digitised.") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

# Envelope gate: the structural check is the typical-value one above.
stopifnot(all(abs(wk26_cohort$median / ref_fig4[wk26_cohort$group] - 1) < 0.25))
```

The digitised interquartile ranges in Figure 4 are about -1.55 to -0.73
(insulin) and -1.02 to -0.47 (no insulin). The virtual-cohort medians sit
below the published ones, by about 15% without insulin. Baseline HbA1c is not
tabulated in the paper, so the cohort centres it on the model baseline; the
published simulation presumably used the observed DINAMO baselines. Because
the drug effect scales roughly with baseline HbA1c to the power 3 (2.04 in
Imax plus 1 through the turnover), a baseline 0.25 percentage points higher
would close the gap. The typical-value comparison above is the structural
check; this one is an envelope. The abstract quotes a paediatric
placebo-adjusted decrease of -0.699% at week 26 without stating the insulin
mix; it matches the no-insulin group.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Reference sex.** The Results state that typical values refer to "a
  non-Black, non-Asian, female" subject, but the supplement equation adds the
  sex effect when FEMALE = 1 and Table 3 labels 1.19 as the "Sex = Female
  effect". The model follows the equation: the reference is male and females
  have 1.19-fold CL/F.
* **Outlier residual error.** The PK residual error has a third, additive term
  (SD 353 nmol/L, Table 3 Sigma 3,3) applied only to observations the authors
  flagged as outliers. That flag is a property of the fitted data set, so the
  model carries only the non-outlier proportional + additive error.
* **Imax covariate form.** The supplement prints IMAX_eGFR = (eGFR/90) x theta
  and IMAX_HbA1c = (HbA1c/7.9) x theta, but its text describes both as
  normalised covariates "with an estimated exponent". The power form is
  used; it reproduces the Figure 4 medians, whereas the multiplicative reading
  would roughly double the drug effect.
* **PROG random effect.** The supplement adds eta3/100000 to the progression
  rate, so the eta is additive and present also in patients without insulin.
  Table 4 prints its magnitude as "CV 7.35%"; the variance is taken as
  log(1 + 0.0735^2) = 0.005388 by the table footnote (0.0735^2 = 0.005402
  differs by 0.3%). The eta is named `etadp_slope` without the log prefix
  of `ldp_slope` because it does not act on the log scale.
* **PROG-BASE off-diagonal.** Table 4 labels 0.00112 "Covariance on
  PROG-BASE" under a "Corr" heading; it is used as the covariance
  (correlation 0.095). Read as a correlation it would be 1.3e-05; either
  way the two random effects are nearly independent.
* **Disease progression.** dkin/dt = PROG with kin(0) = BASE x kout is
  integrated in closed form, kin = BASE x kout + PROG x t, so simulations must
  start at the baseline HbA1c observation (t = 0).
* **Time units.** The model runs in hours; kout is stored in its Table 4 unit
  (1/day) and divided by 24. Figure 2's hour axis and the %/h/h unit of PROG
  confirm hours.
* **Molecular weight.** Concentrations and AUC are in nmol/L and nmol*h/L;
  the paper does not print the molecular weight. 450.91 g/mol
  (C23H27ClO7) is used, as in the other empagliflozin models in this package.
* **Virtual cohorts.** Covariate distributions are reconstructed from the
  summary statistics of Tables S1 and S2; baseline HbA1c is not tabulated in
  the paper and is set to each patient's model baseline. The paper's own
  simulation cohorts are not described in detail, so the comparisons with
  Figures 3 and 4 use the median and are gated at 15% (Figure 3) and 25%
  (Figure 4 cohort); the deterministic typical-value check against Figure 4
  is gated at 10%.
* **Errata.** No erratum was found (literature check 2026-11-05).
